thread:
amy (AMY Sales): quick sync for ACME POC - requirement: private deploy, no public egress. They want guidance: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering, firewall rules we can hand to netsec, TLS-inspect implications, and a POC cost ballpark (2 weeks, ~5k req/day, ~50GB/day). @lina @devon @sanjay

lina (Solutions Eng): short: PrivateLink = simpler firewall story (only outbound to interface ENIs). Peering = L3 access, preserves source IPs, more route work. I'll draft two mini-diagrams + POC pricing one-pager.

devon (Network Eng): network notes: PrivateLink consumers must allow outbound to our ENI CIDRs (we'll provide exact ranges). Peering requires route table updates and no transitive routing. If they need source-IP for logging/IDS, prefer Peering or put a proxy that preserves src. Example firewall snippet: ALLOW TCP 443 to <REDWOOD-ENI-CIDR> ; ALLOW UDP 53 to internal DNS.

sanjay (Security): TLS inspection must be done on customer side. We support mTLS and customer-managed KMS for Private. Security bundle I'll supply: SOC2, POC dataflow, KMS notes, TLS/mTLS options, pen-test summary. Turnaround ~2-3 business days after questionnaire.

amy (AMY Sales): action items: ask customer which connectivity they prefer, whether they'll TLS-inspect, if source-IP is required, and to return the security questionnaire. I'll flag egress-cost concern and request infra credits for POC from sales-ops.

deploy-bot: created INF-8245 to track POC private-deploy network prep (assignee: devon).
